title: Describe a page's protection
description:
Tools that show memory regions describe each page's protection in a short form, the way Linux's `/proc/maps` and many debuggers do: three characters for read, write and execute, using a letter when allowed and `-` when not.

Write `describe(protection)` for these Windows protection values:

| Constant | Value | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `PAGE_NOACCESS` | `0x01` | `"---"` |
| `PAGE_READONLY` | `0x02` | `"r--"` |
| `PAGE_READWRITE` | `0x04` | `"rw-"` |
| `PAGE_WRITECOPY` | `0x08` | `"rw-"` |
| `PAGE_EXECUTE` | `0x10` | `"--x"` |
| `PAGE_EXECUTE_READ` | `0x20` | `"r-x"` |
| `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE` | `0x40` | `"rwx"` |
| `PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY` | `0x80` | `"rwx"` |

The value may also have modifier flags added in its higher bits, such as `PAGE_GUARD` (`0x100`) or `PAGE_NOCACHE` (`0x200`): ignore everything above the low 8 bits. If `PAGE_GUARD` is present, append `" guard"`. For any other low-byte value, return `"???"`.
hints: `protection & 0xFF` keeps the low byte. A `switch` on it, with two `case` labels sharing a result where needed, maps each value to its text.
Check the guard bit (`0x100`) separately, after the main part is decided.
